answer: In a Wesolowski VDF scheme, each identity must complete a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings before its proof is accepted. Domain-separated labels such as lotus, nectar, and summit prevent proofs from being reused across identities. An attacker can run clone chains in parallel, including on GPUs, but cannot parallelize the dependent squarings within any one chain to reduce its elapsed time; each additional clone therefore incurs its own time-bound computation.
